text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - reserved-pool resv-prod-7 is saturated. queue_growth=+420, throttling at route=dedi-enterprise, impacted tenants: [AcmeHealth, NovaBank]. Autoscaler attempted scale_up but rejected: rate_limit. Runbook: /runbooks/reserved-pool-surge

tariq: acknowledging, I'm taking the lead. oncall-tariq. ETA 2m.

maria: I'm looking at autoscaler logs now. grabbing node metrics.

sam: linking dashboards — https://console/redwood/pools/resv-prod-7
- avg token latency spike at 23:11:17
- active sessions: 312 -> 740 in 6m
- queue length: 8 -> 420

maria: autoscaler shows repeated "scale_up rejected: rate_limit" from cloud quota check. also seeing repeated ephemeral eviction loops.

jen: are we hitting the reserved cap (hard cap) or autoscaler rate limits? need to know whether we can just bump max_nodes.

maria: reserved GPUs fully allocated to resv-prod-7 (reservation-count=24). autoscaler trying to request ephemeral nodes but cloud errors 429. Seems cloud provider rate-limiting our scale requests.

tariq: immediate mitigations: 1) apply backpressure to non-critical tenants 2) route enterprise fallbacks to hosted pool 3) evict idle sessions from noisy_tenant if safe. I'll coordinate.

sam: tagging noisy tenant suspect: NovaBank had 48 long-lived streaming sessions started at 23:08. pattern: continuous small-token streaming, no prefix caching.

ops-runner: running quick evict command for idle sessions (dry-run then apply).
```
# evict idle sessions for tenant
rbctl sessions evict --tenant NovaBank --pool resv-prod-7 --idle-threshold 60s --dry-run
```

ops-runner: dry-run shows ~120 sessions eligible. executing now.

ops-runner: applied evict -- now 120 sessions terminated (grace 10s). queue dropped to 310.

maria: nice, small improvement. still high.

dana: I can temporarily raise the autoscaler request rate window to avoid the 429 backoff (infra toggle). But we need cloud approval for more ephemeral nodes — that could take 20-30m. Recommend routing some traffic to fallback models in hosted catalog.

jen: @cs-rep please notify AcmeHealth and NovaBank that we're actively mitigating. tell them potential short-lasting degraded throughput; will follow up.

cs-rep: pinged both customers via support channel. AcmeHealth SL acknowledged, NovaBank asked for ETA. told them ~30m to full mitigation.

tariq: action list I'm executing now:
- enable routing policy fallback: dedi->hosted for route=dedi-enterprise (30% initial)
- evict idle/noisy sessions (done)
- increase autoscaler window (dana)
- open vendor support ticket for cloud rate_limit (sam)

sam: created support case #CS-99881 requesting temporary quota/rate exceptions. linked logs.

maria: pushing a targeted placement policy for AcmeHealth to move to resv-prod-3 (has 6 spare GPUs) by migrating 12 sessions gradual. planning 1m batch.

ops-runner: executing placement migration script:
```
rbctl migrate --from resv-prod-7 --to resv-prod-3 --tenant AcmeHealth --batch-size 12
```

ops-runner: first batch moved 12 sessions. queue dropped to 220. token lat ~180ms -> 120ms on migrated sessions.

tariq: good. doubling down on fallback routing to hosted for non-SLA traffic. applying route patch now.

maria: note — eviction and migration are increasing CPU on control plane but netting good throughput improvement.

incident-bot: automation: applied fallback routing policy (dedi->hosted) for route=dedi-enterprise, initial weight hosted=0.3.

dana: autoscaler window increased (infra-toggle id infra/req-window). temporary max_ephemeral_nodes bumped by +6 (will expire in 1h). monitoring cloud responses.

sam: cloud support responded: investigating rate limit; advised to space API calls. gave tentative 25m ETA.

tariq: current status: queue_length=120, active_sessions=280, throttled_requests down 70%. customers with highest impact moved or on hosted fallback.

jen: who's owned post-incident comms and RCA? I can start draft. need timeline and customer impact numbers.

cs-rep: compiled impact: AcmeHealth ~1200 requests delayed (>2s) during spike window 23:08-23:30; NovaBank had 600 requests and 48 streaming sessions evicted with brief disconnects. Both reported degraded latency.

maria: logging snippets (relevant):
```
2026-03-14T23:09:01Z autoscaler: request_scale_up nodes=6 pool=resv-prod-7 status=429 rate_limit
2026-03-14T23:09:42Z allocator: eviction candidate tenant=NovaBank sessions=48 idle=false
2026-03-14T23:10:15Z router: apply_fallback route=dedi-enterprise weight_hosted=0.3
```

tariq: declaring this as a SEV-2. we'll run through postmortem tomorrow. immediate mitigation stable, keeping page open until cloud confirms rate limit cleared.

dana: cloud responded — temporary exception granted to allow +8 ephemeral nodes, apply within 3m. applying now.

ops-runner: added 8 ephemeral nodes; cluster capacity reflected. queue dropped further to 42.

sam: monitoring shows latencies returning to baseline. routing weight to hosted scaled back to 0.1 to avoid unnecessary cost.

jen: opening incident ticket INC-2026-323 in internal tracker, assigning to 'infra' and 'serving-runtime'. drafting notification to affected customers.

maria: postmortem action items so far:
- add autoscaler exponential backoff jitter tune for cloud 429s
- improve noisy-tenant detection alerting (streaming session pattern)
- add runbook step to route-to-hosted fallback automatically when reserved-pool queue > 200
- CS playbook to notify customers at threshold > 10% of their active sessions impacted

cs-rep: customers acknowledged temporary degraded performance; both requested postmortem. scheduled customer sync for 2026-03-17 16:00 PT.

tariq: leaving monitoring on. if anything regresses i'll re-open page. great teamwork everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident update: SEV-2 mitigated, queue reduced to 42, fallback routing active=0.1, autoscaler max_ephemeral_nodes=+8 (temp). Next: postmortem owner jen, follow-up CS sync scheduled.

ops-runner: adding runbook note: if autoscaler 429s persist, fallback to manual placement migration and customer routing.

jen: posting preliminary incident summary to #postmortems after wrap up.

maria: one more monitoring note: keep cluster margin >=10% to avoid immediate refill. I'll add alert.

tariq: closing page for now. leaving thread open for any follow-ups.
